summary: Normalize pre-existing ADR headings so the canonical adr-shape verifier recognizes Context, Decision, and Consequences sections during local CI mirror verification.
claim_boundary: This is a verifier-unblocker for section-shape metadata and short consequence summaries only. It does not change the substantive decisions, statuses, owners, enforcement lanes, or rollout commitments in the affected ADRs.

source_basis.use: Accepted adr-shape example with exact Context, Decision, and Consequences headings.
Accepted adr-shape example validated by the same local adr-shape command.
Operating contract requiring canonical local verify and ADR doctrine preservation.

findings: The change is minimal heading normalization plus concise consequence summaries; no tool, lane, or runtime code path changes.
Canonical local CI mirrors must be able to enforce ADR shape deterministically; exact headings reduce false-negative policy enforcement in agent workflows.
The previously failing ADRs now pass per-file adr-shape checks alongside the known-good ADR-0321 and ADR-0351 examples.
F3_adversarial.not_applicable_reason: This repairs a shape-validation mismatch rather than a runtime defect; the validator command itself is the regression proof.
F3_adversarial.passing_fixture_id: adr-shape checks for ADR-0321, ADR-0322..0327, ADR-0347, and ADR-0351
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Each changed ADR exposes required Context, Decision, and Consequences sections.

findings: Future agents can inspect affected ADRs through canonical section names instead of special-casing Decision Summary or letter-prefixed headings.
The repair targets the exact D-7 canonical verify failure and keeps the added prose short enough not to alter ADR decisions.
Chose to normalize affected headings instead of weakening adr-shape validation or bypassing advisory verification.
alternatives_named: Ignore D-7 because mandatory gates passed
Normalize affected ADR headings to the validator contract
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Normalizing headings preserves enforcement and avoids verifier bypass while leaving ADR substance intact.
rejected_reasons: Ignoring the failure would leave ./bin/oya verify --ci-required red.
Relaxing the validator would reduce governance signal for future ADRs.

findings: No secrets, tenant data, credentials, policies, or executable security controls are modified.
No runtime path or build-time heavy operation is introduced; docs-only shape normalization has no service performance impact.
The change improves governance compliance by restoring adr-shape recognizability for active doctrine ADRs without changing their policy substance.
Reverting restores the prior headings and removes short consequence summaries; no code, schema, or generated artifacts depend on this change.
No telemetry is added; observability impact is limited to clearer verifier diagnostics and audit-chain evidence for the docs repair.
Existing inbound citations and heading anchors for deeper lettered subsections remain intact; only top-level section headings are normalized.
Top-level headings now use the canonical ADR section names expected by adr-shape.
Affected ADRs keep their existing status, owner, related-spec, and enforcement metadata while satisfying required Context/Decision/Consequences sections.
The changes are confined to docs/decisions plus this evidence/audit-chain record.
No architecture decision is amended beyond surfacing its existing decision/consequence content under canonical headings.
No dependencies or generated clients are added.
No schema or algorithm changes; this aligns markdown headings with an existing shape validator.
The change directly repairs a failing canonical local verify lane, and the full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required command must be rerun before commit.
Challenged whether the right fix was to skip advisory D-7; rejected because ADR shape is part of the canonical local CI mirror and was cheaply repairable.
M1_challenge_assumption.assumption: advisory-looking verifier failures can be ignored

findings: The docs repair is intentionally secondary to the microservice slice; it exists only to keep the branch's canonical verify path honest before shipping.
M2_zoomed_out_fit.fit: verify unblocker for active microservice branch
